The UK constitution is not written in a single document. The UK is a **constitutional monarchy**: the monarch is head of state, but the elected government makes decisions.

**Parliament** has two Houses. The **House of Commons** has elected MPs. The **House of Lords** is not elected and includes life peers, some hereditary peers and senior bishops.

A general election is held at least every **five years**. The **Speaker** chairs debates in the Commons and stays neutral.
key_facts: Constitution: not written in one document
General election at least every five years
